name: POST /api/sla/evaluate - Run the SLA monitoring sweep against ProjexCloud sdk-sla
description: Runs the SLA monitoring sweep: asks ProjexCloud sdk-sla for the authoritative clock verdict on every lead with a running response clock, then records what it learns - setting leads.sla_breached and sla_breach_reason for a breach and writing an observation row to sla_metrics for analysis. ESCALATION: the sweep also raises SLA alerts, reported as alerts_raised and alerts_delivered. An at_risk lead warns its OWNER (owner_warning) while the clock is still running; a breached lead additionally escalates to every active MANAGER (manager_breach). Both tiers are attempted for a breached lead rather than only the manager one, because a lead that ran from on_track straight past its deadline between two sweeps would otherwise never warn its owner at all. Alerts are idempotent per (lead, recipient, tier), so alerts_raised is 0 on a repeat sweep even while the at_risk and breached counts stay the same - that is the anti-spam guarantee, not a missing escalation. Alerting NEVER fails the sweep: an undetected breach is worse than an undelivered notification, so a notification error is recorded on the alert row and the sweep's own findings are still committed. See GET /api/sla/alerts for the ledger and POST /api/sla/alerts/dispatch for the retry path. A command that changes state without creating an addressable resource, so it answers 200 (MUST-54). sdk-sla is the authority because the real deadline runs on a business calendar - working hours, holidays, timezone and pause windows - which LeadFlow does not hold. When the gateway is unconfigured the sweep falls back to a plain wall-clock comparison against sla_due_at and reports clock_source local_wallclock; the fallback exists so a breach is still detected during an outage, and it is NOT a reimplementation of the business calendar, which is why every observation records WHICH clock produced it. monitor_delivered reports whether the sweep reached sdk-sla at all. IDEMPOTENT: re-running changes nothing for a lead already marked breached, and newly_breached lists only the leads whose breach this call discovered - so an alerting job can drive off that list without re-notifying on every pass. A breach is never cleared by a later sweep: a missed deadline is a historical fact. Pass lead_id to evaluate a single lead (the targeted path an operator or a webhook uses); omit it to sweep every lead with an open clock, oldest first, up to limit. QA: depends on register, login and a captured lead - intake auto-routing gives that lead a running clock for the sweep to evaluate.

transitions.notes: At least 80 percent of the response window has elapsed with first_response_at still null. Advisory - reported in the counts and by GET /api/sla/status, but no column changes, so the escalation ladder can warn before the deadline rather than after it.

sla_due_at has passed with no first response. Sets leads.sla_breached true and sla_breach_reason no_response_in_window, writes the observation to sla_metrics, and adds the lead to newly_breached exactly once.
Idempotent no-op. The lead stays breached and does NOT reappear in newly_breached, so an alerting job driven off that list does not re-notify on every sweep.

testCases.name: Evaluate the captured lead's response clock
Reject a lead_id that is not a UUID

errorCases.when: lead_id is present but not a well-formed UUID, or limit is present and not an integer between 1 and 500
the Authorization header is absent, or present without a Bearer token
the bearer token fails verification or has expired
lead_id is a well-formed UUID that no lead holds
